title: Eliminate repeated agent preparation on interactive turns
description:
As a runtime integrator, I want prewarmed agent configuration and optional steering behavior to be honored exactly, so that short interactive turns do not repeat avoidable preparation.

Feature: Reusable interactive agent preparation

Scenario: Agent-level model controls match prewarming
Given an agent declares reasoning effort and verbosity
And the same model stack was prewarmed
When the agent begins a turn
Then it reuses the prewarmed model and adapter
And does not initialize the LM during the request

Scenario: Steering is disabled for a directly driven interactive agent
Given an agent is configured with steering disabled
When it begins a turn
Then it does not query the chat recorder for mid-run steering messages
And it still responds to the directly supplied user message.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Implemented supported steering_enabled Agent configuration and corrected agent-level reasoning/verbosity precedence so prewarm and request-time model keys remain identical. This removes the Console consumer's repeated remote steering lookup without a monkeypatch. Verification: 120 focused tests passed; full unit gate 4,186 passed, 73 skipped, 63 deselected; Behave 449 scenarios passed, 5 skipped; Black and Ruff pass. Sandbox visible benchmark improved from 15.155s before the fixes to 7.596s fresh and 7.268s mean over ten warm turns; LM initialization is absent during requests and provider first chunk is normally 1.65-2.1s. Remaining latency is runtime construction plus sandbox claim/poll overhead, not lazy LM setup.

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Hosted PR checks are also green on Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12 for commit 5b5c0817. PR #93 is clean and mergeable; normal reviewer approval remains the only gate before landing and release.
